# Dimension 4: Token Overhead & Performance

Context cost of tool definitions, structured output overhead, and comparison to
prompt-based enforcement.

## Tool Definition Token Costs

From official documentation and third-party measurements:

| Component | Token Cost | Source |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Simple tool definition | 200-500 tokens (est.) | Multiple community measurements |
| Complex tool definition | ~1,000 tokens | Community measurements |
| `input_examples` (simple) | ~20-50 tokens per example | [4] |
| `input_examples` (complex nested) | ~100-200 tokens per example | [4] |
| Base system prompt for tool use | 313-346 tokens | Community measurements (varies by model) |

## Structured Output Overhead

| Component | Overhead | Source |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| Injected system prompt | ~50-200 tokens (est.) | [1] — "slightly higher" input token count |
| Grammar compilation (first request) | 100-300ms latency | [36] |
| Grammar cache duration | 24 hours | [1] |
| Overall cost increase | ~2-3% | [1] |

Changing `output_config.format` invalidates prompt cache [1]. Changing only `name` or
`description` does not [1].

## Prompt Caching Economics

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Cache hit cost | 90% less than normal input tokens | Anthropic docs |
| Cache write cost | 25% more than normal input tokens | Anthropic docs |
| Break-even point | ~3 cache hits per write | Calculated |
| Standard TTL | 5 minutes | Anthropic docs |
| Extended TTL | 1 hour (at 2x input price) | Anthropic docs |

Tool definitions are cacheable, making the per-request overhead amortizable across
conversation turns [1].

## Approach Comparison

| Approach | Latency Added | Token Cost | Reliability |
|----------|--------------|------------|-------------|
| Prompt-only constraint | +0ms | Schema in system prompt (~200-500 tokens) | 80-95% [16] |
| JSON Mode | +50ms | Similar to prompt | 95-98% [16] |
| Tool use (non-strict) | +0ms (after first) | Tool definition (~200-500 tokens) | 95-99% [16] |
| Strict tool use | +100ms | Tool definition + compilation | <0.1% failure [16] |
| Constrained decoding (FSM) | +1-2s first compile | +0 tokens | 100% [16] |

The Instructor retry pattern adds 200-500ms per retry plus full API call cost [16].

## Token Overhead in Multi-Turn Agents

Tool definitions are re-sent on every turn in multi-turn conversations. At turn 10,
previous 9 turns plus new one are sent — tool definitions included each time.

Anthropic's Tool Search feature addresses this via deferred loading, reducing initial
context consumption. MCP tools are now deferred by default.

## JSON Output Token Overhead

JSON structure itself carries token overhead vs free-form text. One analysis measured
35 tokens for JSON vs 11 tokens for pipe-delimited format for the same 4-field extraction
(3.18x multiplier) [16]. This overhead applies to both prompt-based and schema-based
approaches.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published token count for the StructuredOutput synthetic tool definition specifically
- No controlled A/B comparison of identical schema via tool definition vs system prompt
  instruction with exact token measurements
- Compilation latency varies by schema complexity — the 100-300ms range is approximate
- Ajv validation overhead (~4ms cached, ~110ms uncached) is separate from API latency [10]
